question:
A 70-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer and bone metastases, along with compression
fractures, presents with severe, worsening pain. Despite progression of her disease and treatment with
chemotherapy, she has been taking maximum doses of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, high
doses of extended-release morphine every 12 hours, and high doses of immediate-release morphine
every 4 hours as needed. Recently, she has required immediate-release morphine at least every 2
hours, but her pain remains severe (rated at least 8 out of 10) constantly. The pain is primarily localized
to her bones. She is cachectic, with minimal subcutaneous fat, but denies nausea or vomiting and has
mild constipation controlled with a stool softener. Her kidney function is normal. What is the most
appropriate next step in managing this patient’s pain? Answer Choices: (A) Switch the
extended-release morphine to a low-dose transdermal fentanyl patch every 72 hours (B) Add a
high-dose transdermal fentanyl patch while continuing current morphine regimen (C) Switch to
sustained-release oxymorphone (D) Start oral oxycodone with naloxone combination (E) Initiate
continuous intravenous morphine infusion (F) Begin ketamine infusion while maintaining current opioid
regimen (G) Add gabapentin for bone pain management (H) Switch to oral hydromorphone with
breakthrough doses (I) Increase the dose of the extended-release morphine (J) Switch the
extended-release morphine to methadone
 A. Add gabapentin for bone pain management
B. Switch to sustained-release oxymorphone
C. Switch to oral hydromorphone with breakthrough doses
D. Increase the dose of the extended-release morphine
E. Switch the extended-release morphine to methadone
F. Begin ketamine infusion while maintaining current opioid regimen
G. Switch the extended-release morphine to a low-dose transdermal fentanyl patch every 72 hours
H. Start oral oxycodone with naloxone combination
I. Initiate continuous intravenous morphine infusion
J. Add a high-dose transdermal fentanyl patch while continuing current morphine regimen
